value.title: Multiletter Marton achievability
value.objective: Determine whether finite-letter Marton coding can improve half-skew BSSC achievable sum rates and rigorously characterize structural restrictions on candidate multiletter witnesses.

value.title: Product-code quotient local geometry
value.summary: Analyze exact local optimality and curvature of randomized-time-division tensor points within precisely specified finite-dimensional two-letter Marton architectures.
conditions: Identification of the tensor point and its value with the exact one-use randomized-time-division optimizer requires the accepted result in transaction 88a1004f309460f3ec1cacdae88d30f88559f9bc.

value.title: Strict local maximum in the two-letter product-code quotient
value.summary:
Accepted statement:

For the governed two-use half-skew BSSC, fix W and X^2 to four symbols and the four deterministic product-code orientations (U,V)=(X^2,0),(2X_1,X_2),(X_2,2X_1),(0,X^2), and vary only the 16 positive masses q(W,X^2). At the tensor product of the exact one-use RTD optimizer, whose 4x4 mass matrix has entries (11-sqrt(105))/120, 1/30, and (11+sqrt(105))/120 in the displayed symmetry pattern, the half-weight Marton functional L_{1/2} has constant gradient and a negative-definite Hessian on the full 15-dimensional simplex tangent space. A standard-library checker works exactly in Q(sqrt(105)), verifies all 15 gradient log-product identities, and gives an exact LDL^T decomposition with 15 strictly negative pivots and exact reconstruction. Hence this tensor point is a strict local maximum in the stated fixed-map quotient; its value is 2 L_RTD, and every distinct sufficiently close law in this quotient has selected-law Marton value below 2 L_RTD because min(E_Y,E_Z) <= L_{1/2}. This local theorem does not rule out distant points, directions activating other (W,U,V,X^2) atoms, stochastic or different maps, larger auxiliaries, a two-letter Marton gain in another architecture, Marton additivity, or a capacity converse.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The result applies only to the open 16-cell quotient with the four specified deterministic product-code maps and variation solely of the positive masses q(W,X^2).
- It does not establish global optimality even within that quotient.
- It does not address distant points, activation of other atoms, stochastic or different maps, larger auxiliaries, other two-letter architectures, Marton additivity, or a capacity converse.

value.title: Exact stationarity and tangent-Hessian proof
value.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim. At the interior tensor point, entropy differentiation and the one-use stationary relation establish a constant gradient across the 16 cells. The seven entropy marginal maps give the exact Hessian in Q(sqrt(105)); restriction to the 15-dimensional simplex tangent space followed by an exact LDL^T decomposition with 15 negative pivots proves negative definiteness and hence strict local maximality. The required accepted one-use randomized-time-division result identifies the tensor point's value as 2 L_RTD. Continuity and min(E_Y,E_Z) <= L_{1/2} then give the claimed strict inequality for distinct sufficiently close laws in this fixed-map quotient. This proof item has only the local and architectural scope of the linked accepted claim.

value.title: Exact quadratic-field stationarity and LDL audit tool
value.summary: Standard-library checker used for the exact audit of the linked accepted claim. It works in Q(sqrt(105)), verifies the specified product-code orientations and interior tensor point, constructs all seven entropy marginal maps, checks all 15 tangent gradient log-product identities exactly, forms the full 16-by-16 Hessian, and verifies exact reconstruction of a tangent-space LDL^T decomposition with 15 strictly negative pivots. It certifies only the stated fixed-map local theorem and does not test global optimality, other atoms or maps, larger auxiliaries, Marton additivity, or capacity.

placementAudits.rationale: The accepted claim is a narrowly scoped local-optimality theorem for a fixed two-letter Marton product-code architecture, so it belongs directly in the existing multiletter Marton achievability program rather than at the canonical root or in a converse program.
